control_name: Session Lifetime and Idle Timeout Enforcement
description: Enforce absolute session lifetime limits and idle inactivity timeouts on all authenticated sessions to minimize the window during which a stolen or abandoned session token can be reused. The control requires: (1) an absolute maximum session duration (e.g., 8-12 hours) after which the session is invalidated regardless of activity, forcing re-authentication; (2) an idle timeout (e.g., 15-30 minutes) that invalidates sessions after a period of no activity; (3) server-side session invalidation on explicit logout that destroys the session record rather than merely clearing the client cookie; and (4) session invalidation on security-relevant account changes (password change, privilege escalation, MFA enrollment) to prevent continued use of pre-change session tokens. Configuration is enforced via application server session-timeout directives (web.xml, Tomcat session-config, Django SESSION_COOKIE_AGE, Rails session_store expire_after), reverse proxy session modules (mod_session MaxAge), or identity provider token lifetime policies (Keycloak/RHSSO access token lifespan, SSO session idle/max settings).

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: Session tokens discovered post-hoc (in server logs, backup files, breach data, or browser history) are likely already expired due to absolute lifetime and idle timeout limits — the attacker cannot use stale tokens at leisure. For real-time token theft (XSS exfiltration, MITM), the compressed validity window forces the attacker to maintain persistent real-time access and automated replay infrastructure rather than casually replaying a token hours later. However, automated exploitation can complete within milliseconds of real-time token capture, so the protection is strongest against delayed or historical token reuse and weakest against automated real-time session hijacking

verification.method: Verify that authenticated sessions have both absolute lifetime limits and idle timeouts configured, and that logout explicitly invalidates the server-side session

commands.expected: SESSION_COOKIE_AGE set to 1800 or less (seconds); SESSION_EXPIRE_AT_BROWSER_CLOSE = True
Server-side session invalidation present in logout handler

remediation.name: SSH and shell idle session timeout via sshd drop-in and TMOUT

steps.description: Create sshd drop-in that sends keepalive probes every 300s and disconnects after 3 missed probes (15-minute idle timeout for SSH sessions)
Set a 15-minute shell idle timeout for all login shells via /etc/profile.d drop-in; the shell exits automatically after 900 seconds of inactivity
Reload sshd to apply the ClientAliveInterval drop-in without dropping existing connections

remediation.name: Windows interactive session inactivity timeout via registry policy

steps.description: Set the machine inactivity timeout to 900 seconds (15 minutes) via the local security policy registry key; the lock screen activates after this period of no input
